reason: While the Hebrew midwives (Shiphrah and Puah) do resist Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew male babies by secretly allowing them to live, this does not constitute the regular people being antagonistic to their leader. The midwives' resistance is motivated by fear of God (וַתִּירֶאןָ אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים) rather than antagonism toward Pharaoh. Their defiance is covert and justified on practical grounds (claiming Hebrew women are vigorous and give birth quickly). The broader population (עַמּוֹ - 'ammo, 'his people') shows no evidence of antagonism and, in the final verse, Pharaoh commands them to cast male infants into the river, suggesting obedience rather than opposition. The text presents an act of principled religious disobedience by two officials, not a popular uprising or widespread antagonism.
